input: Look into community land trust housing options

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is for the user personally, a family member, a client, or a community group changes whose needs and eligibility criteria the research must address.
CLTs can be relevant for buying, renting, or developing housing — knowing which use case is intended determines what information to gather.
CLTs are locally operated, so the specific city, region, or country is essential to identify which organizations and listings actually apply.
Income limits, credit requirements, or a target purchase/rent price range will filter which CLT programs the user is actually eligible for or can afford.
The user may want a general education about how CLTs work, a shortlist of specific CLTs to contact, or a ready-to-apply action plan — each requires a very different depth of research.
Knowing the desired output format — a written summary, a spreadsheet of contacts, a checklist — shapes how the research should be organized and delivered.
Some users prioritize homeownership and equity-building, others prioritize low monthly costs or community stability — this affects which CLT features and trade-offs to emphasize.

gold.taskTitle: Research community land trust housing options
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to explore community land trust (CLT) housing as a potential housing option, but the purpose, location, and depth of research needed are all unclear.

questions.title: Who is this housing search for?
questions.description: Is this for yourself personally, a family member, a client, or an organization you are advising? This determines whose eligibility, income, and circumstances the research must center on.

questions.title: Are you looking to buy, rent, or develop through a CLT?
questions.description: Community land trusts offer homeownership, affordable rentals, and land stewardship models. Knowing the intended use case focuses the research on the right programs and processes.

questions.title: What city or region should this research focus on?
questions.description: CLTs are locally operated and vary greatly by area. A specific location is essential to identify real, actionable organizations and available units.

questions.title: What is your approximate income or budget range?
questions.description: Most CLT programs have income eligibility thresholds and price points. Knowing a rough range determines which programs are realistically accessible.

questions.title: What does a useful end result look like to you?
questions.description: Are you aiming to deeply understand how CLTs work, get a shortlist of CLTs to contact, or have a step-by-step plan to apply? This defines how thorough and actionable the output needs to be.

questions.title: What format do you want the findings delivered in?
questions.description: Should this be a written summary, a list of contacts and links, a comparison table, or notes you can act on directly? The format determines how the research gets organized.

questions.title: What matters most — low monthly costs, building equity, or community stability?
questions.description: CLTs involve trade-offs between affordability, resale restrictions, and long-term stability. Knowing your top priority shapes which features and programs to highlight.
